candidates.title: Failure-derived memory retrieval is a sufficient cause of persistent failure in self-evolving agents
candidates.reason: Failure-derived vs success-derived memories change content as well as provenance; the proposed swap does not isolate source type from memory semantics/task hardness.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Construct matched-content or counterfactual relabel/swap units so source provenance changes without changing usable content, then test future persistent failure.

candidates.title: Skill memory pruning threshold interacts with task difficulty to cause performance degradation
candidates.reason: The claim is adaptive pruning-threshold selection by task difficulty, which is ordinary hyperparameter/regime tuning rather than an irreducible agent-evolution mechanism.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Reopen only with matched final memory state showing a history-dependent effect that no state-aware pruning baseline can express.

candidates.title: Temporal grounding failures in time-series agents are due to lack of explicit date-awareness in memory retrieval
candidates.reason: Timestamp-aware retrieval versus semantic retrieval is a generic temporal-grounding/retrieval design comparison; persistent self-evolution is not essential to the claimed residual.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Require a persistent-history variable that changes a future prediction after the same temporal information is available to both methods.

candidates.title: Failure-derived memory retrieval as a causal driver of persistent agent failure
candidates.reason: The measured association is grounded, but the causal intervention swaps failure-derived and success-derived content, leaving content quality/task hardness as competing explanations.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Create matched retrieval interventions controlling content semantics, task hardness and retrieval position; preregister the causal contrast before outcomes.

candidates.title: Underspecification in agent memory as a driver of variance and order-dependent performance drops
candidates.reason: Fully specifying memories adds task constraints unavailable to the underspecified condition, so the baseline is not same-information and cannot isolate underspecification as the causal object.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Define a fixed-information specification perturbation or matched memory pair where only ambiguity/constraint encoding differs, then rerun order/variance tests.

candidates.title: Temporal grounding failure in agentic time series analysis: a capability gap independent of model scale
candidates.reason: Temporal grounding capability gaps and explicit grounding tools are generic reasoning/retrieval questions; the proposed paper does not require persistent self-evolution.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Only revisit if longitudinal memory/history creates a matched-current-state residual that static temporal grounding cannot explain.

candidates.title: Pruning-threshold-induced retrieval-surface bifurcation in self-evolving skill memory
candidates.reason: Changing the pruning threshold deterministically changes which skills survive; this is the expected action of a threshold, not a new structural scientific residual.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Require a path-dependent or irreversible effect after matching the final retained-skill set and all observable state.

candidates.title: Task-order-induced memory-construction variance in self-improving agents
candidates.reason: Task order is a plausible structural variable, but the current falsifier allows different final memory libraries, so ordinary current-state differences can explain future behavior.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Match or quotient the final observable memory/state across different histories and test whether future behavior still diverges; otherwise model the causal write path explicitly.

candidates.title: Skill-retrieval-context mismatch as a structural variable in cross-agent skill transfer
candidates.reason: Context-aware versus context-agnostic skill retrieval is standard conditional retrieval/domain adaptation; the baseline intentionally ignores relevant context.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Require an Agent-specific persistent-state constraint that changes a prediction even when the strongest baseline receives the same context.

candidates.title: Failure-derived memory retrieval predicts persistent failure beyond static skill utility
candidates.reason: Controlling for static utility in logs may establish predictive residual, but it cannot support the current causal claim; retrieval source may proxy content/history/task difficulty.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Either narrow the paper to a prospective predictor or add a matched intervention isolating source provenance while holding content and task factors fixed.

candidates.title: Trust-channel memory inflation predicts error beyond retrieval-channel amplification
candidates.reason: A baseline that ignores a trust annotation available to the proposal is not the strongest same-information baseline; a state-aware baseline can simply condition on that annotation.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Show a structural consequence of trust-history that persists after the baseline receives the full trust annotation/history and makes a different ex-ante prediction.

candidates.title: Skill pruning threshold non-monotonicity: optimal pruning depends on task distribution
candidates.reason: Benchmark-specific optimal pruning thresholds varying with task distribution is hyperparameter selection, not a distinct scientific mechanism.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Reopen only with an irreversible/history-dependent effect under matched final memory state, not another adaptive-threshold rule.

candidates.title: Order-Dependent Memory Corruption in Self-Improving Agents
candidates.reason: This targets genuine order/path dependence, but the described rerun does not yet guarantee identical final observable memory/state; order effects may reduce to different constructed memories.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Freeze two histories that yield the same final visible memory content/retrieval state, then measure future behavior under identical probes; alternatively preregister a causal write-path state variable.

candidates.title: Skill Memory Pruning Threshold as a Hysteresis Switch
candidates.reason: Hysteresis after accumulation is potentially paper-level because it predicts history dependence beyond a fixed threshold, but the current falsifier does not enforce an exact final-memory-state match.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: After accumulated-then-pruned and always-pruned histories, content-address and match the final memory bank plus retrieval metadata before future probes; stop if matched states behave identically.

candidates.title: Infrastructure Failure Memory as a Persistent Behavioral Suppressant
candidates.reason: Resolved versus unresolved failure text changes present memory content, so the experiment does not isolate historical exposure from current representation.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Produce distinct histories with the same final visible memory representation/annotation and test whether future infrastructure use still differs.

candidates.title: Memory-Update Scheduling Under Fixed Total Token Budget: Does Update Order Determine Downstream Task Accuracy?
candidates.reason: Update scheduling under fixed budget can reveal path dependence, but varying order may change final memory content; then ordinary state differences explain the result.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Constrain or match the final memory state across schedules, or identify a causal internal state variable whose value predicts the residual prospectively.

candidates.title: Verification-Aware Termination Threshold: Does Early Stopping on Baseline-Relative Gain Trade Off Semantic Validity?
candidates.reason: Changing a termination threshold and measuring semantic-failure trade-offs is ordinary threshold tuning/search calibration.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Require an unexplained structural phase transition or invariant failure that cannot be represented by budget/threshold-aware search models.

candidates.title: Skill Transfer Under Fixed Execution Budget: Does Workflow Memory Outperform Skills When Infrastructure Failures Are Rare?
candidates.reason: Method advantage varying with failure base rate is a regime-specific benchmark comparison; the residual is a selection threshold rather than an agent-evolution mechanism.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Require a persistent-state mechanism or decision object whose prediction differs from the strongest frequency-aware baseline.

candidates.title: Skill-memory pruning as a continual-learning stability-plasticity tradeoff
candidates.reason: The proposed mapping from task similarity to optimal pruning threshold is a standard stability-plasticity/hyperparameter adaptation problem already expressible by continual-learning baselines.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Find an Agent-specific structural constraint that changes the continual-learning prediction under identical information.

candidates.title: Memory-update frequency as a forgetting-control mechanism in self-evolving agents
candidates.reason: Memory-update frequency versus forgetting is a standard continual-learning control variable, and identical memory content across different update frequencies is not guaranteed by the proposed test.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Require matched final state plus a residual that standard nonstationary/continual-learning models cannot express.

candidates.title: Skill-transfer failure as a distribution-shift detection problem
candidates.reason: Tool-use distribution shift predicting skill transfer is a domain-adaptation predictor; the stated residual is a shift threshold, not an irreducible agent-specific mechanism.
candidates.minimum_next_evidence: Require an Agent-specific persistent skill/state constraint that defeats a strongest distribution-shift-aware baseline with the same histories.
